title: Staged shadow-swap and holdout experiments for version-locked model updates
creator: Lena Thompson
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable, low-risk validation flow for promoting new model revisions when customers use version locks (pins). This flow should allow product teams to run short-lived shadow-swaps and holdout experiments that compare a candidate revision against the pinned revision without exposing the entire customer base. We want to combine offline evals, mirror traffic verification, small-scale A/B holdouts, and an automated telemetry gate that enforces rollback thresholds.

Scope:
- Design the experiment templates and rollout phases for version-locked promotions (shadow-swap, mini-swap cohorts, holdout A/B, progressive exposure).
- Define required telemetry signals, data pipelines, and dashboard surfaces for gating.
- Specify safety/cost/latency thresholds and automated actions (pause/rollback/auto-scale).
- Integrate with existing pin config APIs so customers can opt into staged validation.

Out of scope:
- Changes to model serialization or quantization tooling (handled by Model Onboarding team).
- Large-scale customer-wide rollouts (post validation, separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Experiment template available in Console for version-locked updates (UI + API).
Shadow-swap mode mirrors 100% of request traffic to candidate for scoring without affecting responses to end users.
Mini-swap cohorts can be created with configurable weights (e.g., 0.5% / 1% / 5%) and automatic progression rules.
Automated telemetry gate evaluates latency, token-cost delta, and quality regressions (synthetic eval + online SLOs) and enforces pause/rollback when thresholds breached.
Runbook and rollback playbook documented; one internal dry-run completed and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Design & Safety (2 weeks): finalize signals, thresholds, UI wireframes, permission model.
Phase 1 — Shadow-swap (1 week): mirror traffic and collect metrics; candidate is scored in background only.
Phase 2 — Mini-swap cohorts (2 weeks): expose candidate to tiny cohorts with automated progression rules; monitor metrics closely.
Phase 3 — Holdout A/B (2 weeks): 50/50 experiments for non-critical routes to validate user-visible metrics and regression risk.
Phase 4 — Promote/rollback (ongoing): either finalize promotion to pinned revision or rollback with postmortem.
metrics: Regression rate on eval set (top-level QA prompts)
User-facing error rate (client errors / server errors)
Quality delta via holdout LSAT: semantic-similarity score and human review samples
risk_mitigation: Default safety net: immediate pause and automated rollback when latency P95 increases > 2x or user-facing errors increase > 3x.
Quota isolation: mini-swap cohorts limited to cumulative 5% of traffic across all experiments to avoid capacity churn.
Canary resource reservations: allocate burst tokens for candidate models to prevent noisy neighbor impact.
Manual gating for high-impact customers flagged via 'enterprise' label; require PM/SRE approval before any exposure.
